\section*{Question 2}
![](https://cdn.mathpix.com/cropped/11d3be4b-9004-4f4d-8076-efdeacf28472-1.jpg?height=619&width=595&top_left_y=378&top_left_x=765)
At time \(t\), the position of a particle moving in the \(x y\)-plane is given by the parametric functions \((x(t), y(t))\), where \(\frac{d x}{d t}=t^{2}+\sin \left(3 t^{2}\right)\). The graph of \(y\), consisting of three line segments, is shown in the figure above. At \(t=0\), the particle is at position \((5,1)\).
\begin{itemize}
\item[(a)] Find the position of the particle at \(t=3\).
\item[(b)] Find the slope of the line tangent to the path of the particle at \(t=3\).
\item[(c)] Find the speed of the particle at \(t=3\).
\item[(d)] Find the total distance traveled by the particle from \(t=0\) to \(t=2\).
\item[(a)] \(x(3)=x(0)+\int_{0}^{3} x^{\prime}(t) d t=5+9.377035=14.377\)
\[
y(3)=-\frac{1}{2}
\]
The position of the particle at \(t=3\) is (14.377, -0.5).
\item[(b)] Slope \(=\frac{y^{\prime}(3)}{x^{\prime}(3)}=\frac{0.5}{9.956376}=0.05\)
\item[(c)] Speed \(=\sqrt{\left(x^{\prime}(3)\right)^{2}+\left(y^{\prime}(3)\right)^{2}}=9.969\) (or 9.968)
\item[(d)]
\[
\begin{aligned}
\text { Distance } & =\int_{0}^{2} \sqrt{\left(x^{\prime}(t)\right)^{2}+\left(y^{\prime}(t)\right)^{2}} d t \\
& =\int_{0}^{1} \sqrt{\left(x^{\prime}(t)\right)^{2}+(-2)^{2}} d t+\int_{1}^{2} \sqrt{\left(x^{\prime}(t)\right)^{2}+0^{2}} d t \\
& =2.237871+2.112003=4.350(\text { or 4.349 })
\end{aligned}
\]
\end{itemize}
\(3:\left\{\begin{array}{l}1: \text { integral } \\ 1: \text { uses initial condition } \\ 1: \text { answer }\end{array}\right.\)

1 : slope
\(2:\left\{\begin{array}{l}1: \text { expression for speed } \\ 1: \text { answer }\end{array}\right.\)
\(3:\left\{\begin{array}{l}1: \text { expression for distance } \\ 1: \text { integrals } \\ 1: \text { answer }\end{array}\right.\)
